name: Amanda Quintero
episode: The missing name on the stern
life: “I still remember sewing reversible letters onto a marina pennant.” On Friday, near the foot of Harbor Viaduct, Amanda pauses where the machinery overhead makes two people stand close enough to hear each other.
voice: I make marine flags. I suggested one name on each side so a boat leaving and returning tells the whole story.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a washed violet jersey and a pen clipped inside the neckline. Amanda has a wide brow and a narrow jaw, with short black hair swept back. Amanda draws small circles on a tabletop while waiting during a conversation.
personality: Amanda takes a rejection personally for a day and analytically on the second morning. Amanda can be generous with a rival once the first night's sleep has intervened.
agenda: To offer a reversible family pennant.
family: Lane Marsh is Amanda’s cousin. Amanda can always ask for five minutes alone. Lane asks before bringing somebody along. It keeps a conversation between two people from unexpectedly turning into a family committee. Asked about *The trust with a typo*, Lane says, “I am keeping the wrong envelopes for rejection letters.”
connections: Merritt Hart. A flag maker and a bookkeeper practice the spoken name before they put it in different alphabets.
